allow_large: Owner asked for this change (2026-10-08): a new forge.toml runner setting and a forge init option, written into the generated workflow and reported by doctor and close
done_when: forge.toml has a runner setting (default ubuntu-latest, so nothing changes for repos that don't set it) that forge sync writes into every runs-on line of the generated forge.yml; forge init takes it as an option; the generated jobs' steps work on a plain self-hosted Linux runner (uv and Node installed by their setup actions, nothing assumed from GitHub's hosted image); forge doctor and close's check wait say plainly when a pull request's checks have stayed queued with no runner picking them up for several minutes, naming the runner setting; the coordinator guide documents the setting; command tests cover a new repo initialised with a self-hosted runner and an existing repo adopted on an earlier release that sets it and syncs, plus the queued-without-a-runner message with a faked GitHub

findings.body: The entire branch diff adds only this fix record; none of the promised implementation ships. Both generated jobs still hard-code `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` in src/forge/prcheck.py:55 and :76, and init's options have no runner option (src/forge/init.py:19–27). The workflow still assumes system Python before setup-uv (src/forge/prcheck.py:67) and system python3 with tomllib (:113–118), so plain self-hosted Linux support is also unfinished. Close collapses queued and running checks into the same pending state (src/forge/checks.py:68–70), then says they are 'still running' (:57); doctor has no queued-runner diagnosis. Neither the coordinator guide nor shipped coordinator template is updated. Implement every Done-when detail, retaining ubuntu-latest as the default and applying the configured runner to both jobs. Otherwise the reported self-hosted-only organisation remains unable to run these checks.
findings.title: Not done: runner setting, init option, self-hosted workflow support, queued-check diagnostics and coordinator documentation

findings.body: No tests are added for any of the required scenarios: a new repository initialised with a self-hosted runner; an existing client adopted on an earlier release that sets the runner and syncs; and several-minute queued checks reported through both doctor and close with GitHub faked at its boundary. Existing setup coverage checks the test command and PR-check invocation (tests/test_setup.py:128–134), while the queued-check case explicitly expects only 'still running' (tests/test_close.py:299–303). Those cases do not prove the promised behaviour. Add command-level coverage that verifies both generated jobs use the selected runner, preserves the default, checks the required tool setup, and verifies the runner-setting diagnosis from both commands.
findings.title: Not done: command tests for new clients, earlier-release adoption and queued-without-a-runner diagnostics

findings.body: The supplied proof list is explicitly missing, and the branch provides only a start record. Supply the required complete list mapping every Done-when detail to its implementation and named proof, including new-client init, earlier-release adoption and sync, self-hosted tool setup, and doctor/close queued-runner diagnostics. There are currently no entries to audit.
findings.title: Not done: proof list

why: The CI workflow Forge generates hard-codes runs-on: ubuntu-latest for both jobs, so in an organisation whose repos can only use self-hosted runners every new client repo's tests and forge-pr-check jobs stay queued forever, forge close waits on them indefinitely and no item can become ready; checks = [] is no way out because close refuses with no checks (owner report, 2026-10-08)
